scope.question: Which documented organizational factory patterns can inform a repository-native, factory-as-code runtime, and which claims have outcome evidence?
boundaries: Engineering ships first. The design does not claim a universal agent/plugin platform.
GTM is a separate repository and domain configuration. It remains disabled until explicit engineering-maturity and GTM value/risk gates pass.
A documented feature or vendor case is not an audited outcome. Product UI screenshots, testimonials and internal anecdotes are labeled accordingly.
The study compares roles, workflows, artifacts, evals, human gates, domain ownership, cross-repo handoffs and protected improvement. It does not rank foundation models.
scope.time: 2023-present for agent products, with older SRE/standards foundations where relevant; evidence cutoff 2026-09-13.

verified_capabilities.documented: Factory-as-code docs and v1alpha1 schemas cover factory, agent, automation, runner, benchmark task/suite/scorer, skill and webhook definitions (S45-S47). The default workflow is Intake→Triage→optional Planning→human spec approval→Build→Review↔Build→human handoff; Review is advisory and Complete means handed to a human, not merged (S48,S49). Product pages describe foreman orchestration, human gates and human merge (S1). Scorers are LLM classification judges with thresholds/sampling; self-improvement groups 25 failures or the oldest 7 days and opens a config PR for human review (S50,S51).
verified_capabilities.outcome_status: Warp reports an internal 30-task replay costing $2,130.57 and a routing change associated with $80→$30 cost/completed PR and 69%→87% task-compliance score (S2). This is first-party, small, LLM-judged and not audited; no raw benchmark dataset/variance/delayed defect denominator. Docs state third-party harness comparison was unavailable and A/B testing remained future (S2,S52).

verified_capabilities.documented: Claude Research uses a lead orchestrator, parallel subagents, persistent checkpoints/artifacts and a separate citation stage. Anthropic reports an internal 90.2% lift over single-agent on its research eval and up to 90% latency reduction, but about 15× chat tokens and limited suitability for less-parallel coding work (S3). Anthropic’s general patterns are chaining, routing, parallelization, orchestrator-workers and evaluator-optimizer, with advice to begin simply (S4). Agent evals combine outcomes/traces with deterministic, model and human graders, repeated trials, capability vs regression suites and domain-owned tasks (S5).
verified_capabilities.outcome_status: Anthropic reports shared workspace rosters, manual review→task-class earned autonomy, doer/verifier splits, batched questions and explicit human owners (S55), plus an intent→spec→plan→diff/tests→PR→incident artifact playbook (S56). Internal Claude Code use across functions shows domain-specific artifacts (S6). These are selected first-party reports; claims such as “500 fixes” and reported time savings lack complete denominators/audit.

verified_capabilities.documented: Codex cloud supports repository-connected isolated tasks, parallel/background work, tests/diffs and PR handoff; environment setup, secrets removal, default-off internet and layered AGENTS.md are explicit but instructions are not authority (S7,S8,S63-S66). Symphony specifies issue/status as durable identity, one workspace/agent per open task, restart/reconciliation, WORKFLOW.md, CI shepherding and review packets, with humans admitting follow-ups (S61,S62). OpenAI evals/trace grading support task datasets and diagnostic trace evidence (S9,S10).
verified_capabilities.outcome_status: Harness Engineering reports ~1M LOC and ~1,500 merged PRs with 3→7 engineers and extensive docs/structural tests/observability, but allows agent review/self-merge and is an unaudited, unusual greenfield case; it also reports a prior ~20% cleanup burden (S60). Symphony’s “500%” landed-PR increase lacks denominator/defect/reviewer cost (S61). A separate internal trace monitor is evidence for oversight but is asynchronous and first-party (S67).

verified_capabilities.documented: Copilot cloud agent runs research→plan→one repo/branch→code/test→optional PR in an ephemeral Actions environment (documented 59-minute maximum); it cannot ready, approve or merge its PR, and workflow execution normally requires a write-authorized human approval (S12,S68). Custom Markdown-YAML profiles distribute specialist prompts/tools/MCP, but omitted tools default broadly and profiles are neither identities nor approvals (S13,S70). Copilot automations are creator-private and not Git-versioned; confidence approval UI is not a server-side security boundary (S71,S72). Agentic Workflows compiles Markdown to Actions and was public preview (S73). Microsoft’s Agentic SDLC Starter shows reference roles/artifacts (S17).
verified_capabilities.outcome_status: The GitHub billing team reports narrow technical-debt usefulness but hours of human review and warns against 100+-file PRs (S14). No controlled counterfactual/defect denominator. Agentic Workflow testimonials are marketing, and network/firewall coverage excludes some setup/MCP paths (S69,S73).

verified_capabilities.documented: Duo Agent Platform offers catalog, project enablement, custom flows, triggers, sessions and runners (S18-S22,S75). YAML separates Agent, Tool, AI Task and Human Input; publishing and enablement are separate Maintainer/Owner actions (S75). Composite identity intersects initiator/service-account authority for runner flows, not Agentic Chat (S76).
verified_capabilities.outcome_status: Material caveat: runner flows have no present user, do not support Always Ask, and an unspecified tool rule defaults Allow; audit storage/forwarding may be opt-in; “zero retention everywhere” is not supported (S77-S80). Thus background GTM cannot carry publish/send/CRM-write authority and rely on an interactive gate. Documentation establishes mechanics, not outcome/security audit.

verified_capabilities.documented: Cognition describes dogfooding Devin (S23); Answer.AI documents supervision and task-selection limits (S24). METR found experienced maintainers slower with early-2025 tools on familiar repositories despite positive expectations (S25). DORA says AI outcomes depend on the wider delivery system (S26).
verified_capabilities.outcome_status: These conflict with simple vendor productivity narratives and justify local, workflow-level controlled evaluation.

verified_capabilities.documented: GitLab’s public marketing operations/campaign handbook shows DRI, systems-of-record and measurement artifacts (S28,S29). Warp’s open GTM, social and CRO references show evidence-rich account handoffs for rep review, social drafts routed to Slack/human publication, and experiment changes via PR with human prioritization/merge (S81-S86). HubSpot offers designated pre-publication approval objects (S89); Adobe offers versioned brand guidance/approval (S33,S34).
verified_capabilities.outcome_status: CRMArena/Pro report substantial CRM failure and weak inherent confidentiality awareness (S87,S88). FTC/ICO and Gmail make consent/suppression/content/authentication/complaint controls operational gates, not prompt advice (S35,S36,S90). No source establishes generic autonomous GTM lift or safety.

evidence_grade.A: Standards, regulator rules, public source/config behavior (S15-S18,S35-S44).
evidence_grade.B: First-party engineering reports with concrete methods/numbers but no external audit (S2,S3,S14,S23).
evidence_grade.C: Vendor docs/announcements/handbook statements proving intended capability only (S1,S6-S13,S18-S22,S28-S34).
evidence_grade.challenge: Independent study/practitioner evidence (S24-S26), which is credible but scoped to its population/version.

what_is_not_proven: No comparator publishes a third-party audit of a general factory spanning ideation→production→learning.

Warp v1alpha1 defines desired files, not an authoritative live work-item/event/effect store; public RunState is only run status. Prompt-configured review/spec behavior is not authorization enforcement (S45,S46,S48-S50,S54). Factory MCP pickup does not claim/lock/pause work and account access is not per-factory scope (S53).
WarpBench has 30 curated tasks, uses LLM-as-judge, lacks raw runs/confidence intervals/delayed defect data and evaluated retrospective similarity; causal attribution remains uncertain (S2).
Internal use stories omit failed-task denominators, reviewer time, selection policy, opportunity cost and long-term escaped defects (S6,S7,S14,S23).
Configuration and gates prove enforceable mechanics only when the hosting rules, identities and bypass lists are independently reconciled (S15,S16).
GTM tool support does not prove incremental revenue, valid attribution, consent, factual accuracy or brand safety (S28-S37).

Anthropic’s multi-agent research numbers are internal; its human-agent-team and Claude Code reports are selected anecdotes. There is no released task-level replication or full reviewer/cost/defect denominator (S3,S6,S55,S56).

OpenAI’s Harness Engineering and Symphony show a highly instrumented internal environment and high activity, not independently audited quality/value. Agent self-merge/minimal blocking gates conflict with conservative separation and should not transfer by default (S60,S61).
GitHub cloud-agent safeguards and Agentic Workflows controls are documented mechanics, not an independent security/ROI audit; firewall exclusions for MCP/setup steps remain (S68-S73).
Open GTM agent kits prove inspectable workflow/artifact patterns, not real deployment, ROI or compliance; CRMArena results actively challenge unrestricted CRM writes (S81-S88).
evidence_and_limits.measurement_rule: Every claim must bind claim_id→source IDs→factory/version→task cohort→baseline→denominator→human minutes→cost→quality/incident outcomes→measurement window. Label vendor-reported, internally reproduced, independently replicated or audited.
evidence_and_limits.date_caveat: The requested cutoff is 2026-09-13. Living documents were read as current to that cutoff. Future changes after cutoff are excluded; pages with no stable date are marked living.

actors_and_authority.separation: Agents may draft, analyze, test and propose. They cannot approve their own artifact, alter protected evaluators/policy/audit history, expand permissions, spend money, publish externally, bulk-contact people, mutate consent/suppression data, merge protected code or deploy high-risk changes. Path owners and rulesets enforce repository authority (S15,S16); excessive-agency guidance supports minimum tools/permissions (S39). Anthropic’s reported practice adds explicit rosters, one human owner per agent/task class, manual review for new agents and doer/verifier separation (S55). GitHub gives a strong concrete boundary: the cloud agent cannot ready, approve or merge its own PR and attributed requester work cannot self-approve (S12,S68). Custom profiles/agent confidence do not create principals or security approval (S70,S72). GitLab’s composite identity is a useful initiator∩service-account model for background flows, but only where explicitly supported (S76). Its runner tool policy cannot pause for Always Ask and defaults unspecified tools to Allow, so effectful GTM uses a deny-only worker plus separately approved publisher principal (S77).
actors_and_authority.identity: One workload identity per factory/domain/stage, short-lived credentials, explicit repo/channel/CRM object scopes. Human approvals record authenticated principal, role, artifact digest, policy version, decision, expiry and rationale. No shared “agent” superuser.

complete_state_catalog.terminal_rule: SUCCEEDED means the declared artifact contract and gates passed, not that downstream business value is proven. Only SUCCEEDED, CANCELLED, FAILED_FATAL, POLICY_DENIED, APPROVAL_REJECTED, ROLLED_BACK and ARCHIVED are terminal; late events create a reconciliation record rather than silently reopening.

transition_contract.event_envelope: Use CloudEvents fields id/source/type/specversion/time/subject plus project_id, domain, work_id, attempt, factory_version, artifact_refs/digests, correlation/causation IDs, actor identity and policy version (adapted from S41).
guards: actor authorized for action and domain
required approval binds exact digest and is unexpired
transition_contract.effects: Append immutable event; atomically update projection/outbox; mint least-privilege task capability; store content-addressed artifact/provenance; schedule or cancel next stage; emit receipt.
transition_contract.idempotency: Unique (project_id,event_id) and (work_id,transition,attempt,input_digest). Duplicate side effects use destination idempotency keys; external publish/CRM/spend operations require read-after-write reconciliation.
transition_contract.invalidation: Source commit, requirements, brand guide, consent/suppression list, CRM schema, audience, pricing or policy changes invalidate derived artifacts and approvals. Re-evaluate from the earliest affected stage.
transition_contract.reconciliation: Poll authoritative Git/CI/CRM/channel state; compare desired/applied versions; quarantine orphaned runs; recover expired leases; never infer approval from a comment string.

engineering: WORKFLOW.md/status link and visual review packet/video where UI behavior is acceptance evidence (S61)
gtm: ICP/audience definition and allowed data fields
artifact_contracts.boundary: A chat transcript is evidence/context, never the sole contract. A PR/MR, signed approval, manifest or publication receipt is the durable handoff. SLSA-style subject digests and builder identity are adapted beyond builds (S43); JSON Schema validates structure (S42). Anthropic’s SDLC playbook independently converges on intent/spec/plan/diff-tests/PR-review/incident artifacts (S56), but remains guidance rather than audited outcome evidence.

conversation_and_handoffs.interaction: The foreman/supervisor may be one conversational voice, as Warp proposes, but it must not become one authority (S1). Each question becomes a typed NEED record: missing field, choices, recommendation, impact, deadline and safe default. Human response becomes a DECISION artifact bound to affected inputs.
conversation_and_handoffs.checkpoint: After each stage store objective, accepted inputs, open questions, decisions/rationale, artifact digests, remaining budget, leases, next allowed transitions and compacted evidence citations. Resume reloads typed state and verifies source revisions; it does not rely on model memory. OpenAI’s Symphony likewise treats issue/workspace and WORKFLOW.md as durable identity/state rather than a chat session, and can return PRs or analysis/review packets (S61,S62).
conversation_and_handoffs.cross_repo_handoff: Producer repo creates a signed manifest containing schema/version/digests/purpose/data class/requested action/expiry/policy verdict. Broker sends only the manifest and authorized content references. Consumer repo validates, records ACCEPT/REJECT with reason, copies or references immutable artifacts under its retention policy, and emits receipt. No agent receives blanket read/write across both repos.
examples: Engineering→GTM: only an approved release manifest, feature facts, limitations, security/privacy statements and docs digests; not source secrets or speculative roadmap.
GTM→Engineering: aggregated, consent-safe insight/experiment result or a typed product request with evidence; not raw CRM export unless an approved contract requires it.
conversation_and_handoffs.compaction: Summaries must retain claims→sources, dissent, rejected options, approvals, classification and hashes; lossy natural-language summary cannot replace the originals.

orchestration_and_composition.pattern: Use deterministic workflows around bounded agents. Router chooses task class; orchestrator may fan out only independent research/tests; join requires declared quorum/completeness and preserves disagreement. Anthropic’s research system reports strong internal breadth/latency results but ~15× chat tokens and poor fit where coding tasks do not decompose; its general guidance says start simply (S3,S4).
orchestration_and_composition.subfactories: Engineering v1 composes intake→spec→implement→verify→PR→human merge→deploy/observe. Research, review and incident response are bounded subfactories with their own artifacts/evals. GTM later composes research→ICP/positioning→campaign/content→approval→publish/CRM→measure, but remains separately configured.
orchestration_and_composition.budgets: Per work item: wall clock, tokens/cost, tool calls, concurrency, retries and external side effects. Fanout requires estimated marginal value; join cancels stragglers only under a declared completeness policy.
orchestration_and_composition.cleanup: Revoke credentials, stop compute, delete/retain sandbox per policy, release leases, finalize artifact indexes and reconcile external side effects even on cancellation/failure.
orchestration_and_composition.anti_pattern: Do not encode human job titles as endlessly chatting personas. Encode authority, required artifacts, transitions and acceptance tests. Microsoft starter/custom agents are useful templates (S13,S17), not proof that more roles improve outcomes.

deterministic_stop_or_approval: production deploy or protected-branch merge according to local risk tier

all external GTM publication, paid-spend start/increase, new audience activation, personalized outbound, bulk CRM write/delete/merge, consent/suppression mutation, sensitive-data export, brand exception, regulated claim or rights/licensing uncertainty
input changed after approval; approval expired; conflict of interest; retry/budget limit reached; credible prompt injection or secret exposure
human_need_policy.probabilistic_triggers: Local, pre-registered examples—not vendor defaults: ask clarification if calibrated completeness/correctness confidence <0.85; escalate if independent graders disagree by >0.15 probability or any safety grader fails; stop on out-of-distribution score above the validated 99th-percentile threshold; randomly human-audit ≥5% of low-risk successes and 100% during canary. Thresholds must be calibrated per domain/task and never override deterministic safety gates.
human_need_policy.approval_contract: Approver must own the affected domain and see exact artifact digest, diff, evidence/evals, data classes, audience/channel, costs and rollback. No rubber-stamp buttons without context. Two-person approval for permission/policy changes and high-impact GTM actions.
human_need_policy.safe_default: Timeout means pause or cancel, never publish/merge/spend. Human edits invalidate prior scores and rerun affected checks. Model confidence/rationale is an escalation signal only; GitHub explicitly says its approval UI is not the underlying security boundary (S72).

domain_owned: versioned shared automations: reject creator-private/non-reviewed automation storage for production governance; compile/generated workflow must have reviewed source and provenance (S71,S73)
factory_as_code_schema.avoid_premature_universality: Keep one internal v1alpha1 kernel and hard-coded engineering adapter set. Warp’s actual v1alpha1 schemas are a useful desired-configuration reference but explicitly do not supply the live lifecycle/effect store (S45,S46); its examples are young and config-only (S47). Do not promise third-party plugins or a stable cross-domain SDK until two implemented domains expose repeated stable abstractions and compatibility tests.

engineering_first: Authenticated issue/spec trigger; readiness and risk classification.
Human product owner approves ambiguous/high-impact spec.
Controller leases isolated task to implementer; branch-only token.
Implementer produces patch/tests/evidence and draft PR.
Independent verifier rebuilds exact head and runs deterministic, security and stochastic task evals.
CODEOWNER reviews digest-bound diff; ruleset/merge queue enforces checks.
Release owner approves environment where required; canary/rollback are deterministic.
Telemetry creates proposals/postmortems/eval cases; no automatic protected-policy mutation.
gtm_after_activation: Researcher creates sourced market/ICP brief; privacy filter blocks unjustified personal data.
Positioning owner approves claims/message house and prohibited claims.
Campaign DRI creates audience, channel, budget, experiment and attribution plan with baseline and success/stop criteria.
Content agents draft variants against versioned brand/rights/claim artifacts; factual, brand, accessibility, privacy and channel checks run.
Legal/privacy/brand/data steward review exact digests when policy requires. Adobe shows explicit guideline/approval objects; this supports the pattern but not automatic correctness (S33,S34).
CRM writer produces dry-run change set; steward approves; scoped adapter writes with idempotency and stores receipt. Suppression/consent lists are protected (S35,S36).
Publisher previews destination payload; channel owner approves external publication/spend; system stores destination ID/time/rendered capture and rollback/takedown path.

Analyst joins exposure, cost, funnel and revenue outcomes using versioned attribution assumptions; reports incremental lift where experiment supports it, otherwise labels correlation. Complaints, unsubscribes, privacy requests and brand incidents feed stop/learning.
end_to_end_workflows.publication_boundaries: Internal draft and sandbox CRM are automatable. External send/post/ad activation, material budget, regulated/public claims, targeting using personal/sensitive data and production CRM destructive writes are never inferred from “campaign approved”; each is a distinct gate. Never give one web-reading/background agent sensitive CRM plus autonomous send/publish access: GitLab describes that combination as the prompt-injection “lethal trifecta” (S79).
metrics: Engineering: accepted PR rate with denominator, cycle/queue/human time, cost/accepted PR, rework, escaped defects/security findings, rollback/change-failure rate and developer experience.

GTM: research citation coverage, approval/rework latency, brand/claim defect rate, consent/suppression violations=0, send/publish failure, complaint/unsubscribe, qualified pipeline/revenue, incremental lift and confidence interval, CAC/payback, cost per approved artifact—not raw volume or vanity clicks alone.

loop: Human curator turns failure/success into versioned eval case with provenance and privacy review.
Observer may propose a minimal config/prompt/router/tool change as a PR; Warp documents this proposal pattern (S1).
Independent evaluator replays frozen task/environment/config snapshots and fresh holdout/adversarial cases; compare quality, safety, latency, cost and human effort.
Independent owner approves shadow→bounded canary; predeclared abort rules.
Promote immutable version or rollback; measure delayed defects/business outcomes and revert on regression.
protected_invariants: executing agent cannot edit its evaluator, hidden cases, expected outputs, inclusion rules, promotion threshold, permissions/gates, audit/provenance, consent/suppression, legal/brand controls or rollback mechanism
candidate and evaluator identities/data stores separated
no scalar average can compensate for a safety/privacy/legal invariant failure
raw GTM personal data cannot become training/eval data without approved purpose, minimization, retention and deletion path
self_improvement_boundary.promotion: Require no invariant regression, statistically/operationally meaningful improvement on pre-registered metrics, bounded cost, human sign-off and reversible version. Warp’s 25-failure/7-day mechanism opens a config PR and keeps adoption human-reviewed, a transferable proposal pattern but not validated promotion (S51). LLM scorers need independent calibration because Warp documents classification/threshold behavior without a protected grader (S50); WarpBench is hypothesis evidence, not an automatic router mandate (S2,S5,S9,S10).

schema_and_transition: JSON Schema positive/negative fixtures; backward/forward compatibility (S42).
Model-check allowed transitions, terminality and authorization; property tests for duplicate/out-of-order events, stale approvals, lease expiry, cancellation and rollback.
Contract tests for GitHub/GitLab/CRM/channel sandboxes; idempotent replay and read-after-write reconciliation.
security_privacy: Threat-model every repo/web/CRM/email/tool input as untrusted; prompt-injection corpus and egress/secret exfiltration tests (S38).
Least-privilege identity tests; attempts to self-approve, expand tools, read other repo/domain, alter evals/audit or bypass rules must fail (S39).
PII discovery/minimization, consent/suppression, retention/deletion, residency, audit and incident exercises (S35-S37,S40).

For GitLab-like runners test explicit deny for every unspecified effect tool, composite-identity intersection, audit forwarding/storage/readback and retention routing; do not infer these from UI presence (S76-S80).
evaluations: Frozen replay plus time-split fresh/holdout cases; repeated trials and confidence intervals.
Deterministic outcome checks first; trace graders for diagnosis; blinded calibrated human panels for semantic/brand/factual claims (S5,S9,S10).
Adversarial, metamorphic and cross-domain leakage cases; score abstention/escalation precision and false-negative rate.
Compare against no-agent/current workflow and include reviewer time, retries, cost, escaped defects/complaints and delayed outcomes.
acceptance: Engineering pilot: stable event/provenance/audit, zero authority escapes, rollback drill passes, and predeclared workflow metrics improve without quality/stability regression.

GTM pilot: shadow/draft only first; zero consent/publication/spend authority escapes; brand/legal reviewers meet agreement target; controlled experiment shows enough expected value to cover operations/review risk.

implementation_recommendation.decision: BUILD A NARROW DOMAIN-NEUTRAL KERNEL, SHIP AN ENGINEERING FACTORY FIRST, AND DEFER GTM EXECUTION. Do not build a universal factory marketplace/plugin SDK now.
implementation_recommendation.phase_0: Implement shared event/state/artifact/provenance/identity/gate/eval/audit kernel; one GitHub/GitLab adapter; engineering issue→draft PR workflow; protected config repository; dashboards with denominators.
implementation_recommendation.phase_1: Add independent verification, risk-tier gates, deployment/rollback and governed eval→proposal PR loop. Pilot narrow classes such as test maintenance, dependency changes or failing-CI repair, consistent with bounded team cases (S14,S22).
engineering_extraction_gate: ≥2 materially different engineering workflows use the same kernel without copy-pasted controller logic
≥100 accepted/terminal runs across ≥2 repositories and ≥8 weeks (illustrative minimum)
zero unresolved authority/secrets/cross-project isolation escapes; rollback and disaster recovery exercised
event/artifact schema changes stabilized and migration/compatibility tests pass
measured value survives reviewer-time, failure and delayed-quality accounting; owners approve support burden
implementation_recommendation.domain_sdk_gate: Extract only repeated seams—artifact type registry, policy/eval provider interface and adapters—after a second real domain proves them. Keep domain workflow DSL and roles private/unstable before then.
gtm_activation_gate: named GTM, brand, RevOps/data and privacy/legal owners; separate protected repository and identities
one bounded use case with baseline/expected value (e.g., evidence-backed draft content or campaign QA), not autonomous outbound
approved data inventory/lawful-purpose/retention/residency and CRM/channel contracts; sandbox/dry-run available
brand/claim/rights/consent/suppression eval set with human agreement calibration
publication/spend/CRM gates and takedown/reversal drill proven; audit receipt end-to-end
engineering kernel meets extraction gate and cross-repo manifest/receipt isolation tests pass
implementation_recommendation.gtm_first_release: Draft-only research→content package and campaign QA. No personal-data enrichment, automated personalized outreach, auto-publish, budget change or destructive CRM write. Expand one side effect at a time after canary evidence. Earn autonomy by task class after repeated success and sustainable review load, not by granting a repository-wide “trusted agent” status (S55).
implementation_recommendation.buy_vs_build: Use vendor harnesses/runners behind adapters where useful; own authoritative policy, identities, artifacts, eval datasets, approval records and audit. Vendor factory claims (S1,S7,S18) do not justify outsourcing governance.

conflicts.evidence_for: Anthropic reports benefit for broad parallel research but high token cost and limited coding parallelism (S3); vendor platforms expose specialized roles/flows (S1,S13,S17-S22,S55).
conflicts.evidence_against: Anthropic advises simple workflows first (S4); coordination/token costs grow and role diagrams lack outcome proof.
conflicts.resolution: Use fanout only for separable work with a measurable join condition. Prefer typed stage authority over persona count.

conflicts.claim: Factory self-improvement can automatically optimize routing/config.
conflicts.evidence_for: Warp documents replay and grouped-failure proposals as reviewed config PRs, and reports cost/compliance improvements from routing (S1,S2,S51).
conflicts.evidence_against: Small curated retrospective, LLM classification judge without public calibration, no raw data/CI/delayed defects; third-party harness comparison and A/B testing were not available at cutoff (S2,S50,S52).
conflicts.resolution: Observer proposes PR only; frozen plus fresh evals, independent approval, shadow/canary and rollback.

conflicts.evidence_against: METR found a 19% slowdown in its early-2025 scoped RCT; its 2026 follow-up estimates had confidence intervals including zero and serious selection/randomization/time-accounting limits; Answer.AI reports supervision limits (S24,S25,S59). DORA stresses system context (S26).
conflicts.resolution: No universal multiplier. Measure local task cohorts with reviewer time, denominators, quality and delayed effects.

conflicts.claim: One factory abstraction should span engineering and GTM.
conflicts.evidence_for: Both have triggers, actors, artifacts, state, gates, evaluation, provenance and side effects; standards support shared envelopes (S41-S44).
conflicts.evidence_against: Authority, artifact semantics, risk, metrics, data and terminal actions differ sharply; generic agent/chat abstractions hide these differences (S28-S37).
conflicts.resolution: Share the small control-plane kernel only. Keep repositories, schemas, workflows, identities, policies, evals and adapters domain-owned until repeated evidence justifies extraction.

conflicts.claim: Human review makes agent output safe.
conflicts.evidence_for: Warp, GitHub, GitLab and Adobe expose approval/review stops (S1,S11,S15,S16,S21,S34).
conflicts.evidence_against: Review can be rubber-stamped; reviewers need exact digests, independent evidence and enforceable rules. Security/privacy law is not delegated by a UI (S35-S40).
conflicts.resolution: Digest-bound role-authorized gates, independent trusted checks, sampled audit and deny-by-default timeouts.

conflicts.claim: A foreman should be the single voice and authority.
conflicts.evidence_for: Warp’s single reporting voice simplifies interaction (S1).
conflicts.evidence_against: Concentrating approval, execution and evaluation violates separation and creates correlated failure.
conflicts.resolution: One conversational facade is acceptable; retain separate workload identities, policy engine, evaluator and human owners.

conflicts.claim: Human review/merge is always required for agent code.
conflicts.evidence_for: Warp and GitHub default to human handoff/review plus repository enforcement (S11,S12,S15,S16,S48).
conflicts.evidence_against: OpenAI’s internal Harness Engineering permits mostly agent-to-agent review and sometimes agent self-merge, reporting high throughput in a heavily instrumented greenfield repository (S60).
conflicts.resolution: Treat this as a context-specific exception, not general proof. Engineering v1 requires independent trusted checks and risk-tier human merge/deploy. Any later relaxation needs task-class evidence, isolation, sampled human audit, incident budget and rapid rollback.

conflicts.claim: Background-flow human-input/tool “ask” gates protect external effects.
conflicts.evidence_for: GitLab custom flows define optional Human Input and interactive governance supports Always Ask (S75,S77).
conflicts.evidence_against: GitLab explicitly says runner flows have no present user, do not apply interactive human-in-loop, support Allow/Deny only and default unspecified rules to Allow (S77).
conflicts.resolution: Worker identity has deterministic deny for publish/send/spend/CRM mutations. A durable digest-bound approval triggers a separate least-privilege effect executor; timeout/unspecified means deny.

conflicts.claim: GTM agents can safely automate CRM and publication with prompts/review.
conflicts.evidence_for: Warp/HubSpot/Adobe expose draft, review and handoff workflows (S33,S34,S81-S89).
conflicts.evidence_against: CRMArena-Pro finds low CRM reliability/confidentiality awareness; regulator/provider duties and prompt-injection risks remain (S35,S36,S79,S87,S88,S90).
conflicts.resolution: Read/analyze/draft first. CRM dry-run patch sets and external effects require deterministic compliance checks and separate authorized humans/executors; expand only by task class after measured canary evidence.

uncertainties.unknown: Warp Factories used v1alpha1 config schemas at cutoff. Public docs covered desired files and a prompt-configured workflow, but not a complete authoritative live event/effect store or hard enforcement semantics (S45-S54).
uncertainties.impact: High for buy/build and interoperability; treat examples as vendor claims until pilot/contract test.

uncertainties.unknown: No raw data or independent replication for WarpBench and most internal team cases; total failed runs, reviewer time and delayed defects are absent.
uncertainties.impact: High; cannot infer causal ROI or safe automation percentage.

uncertainties.unknown: Probability thresholds and audit sample rates are illustrative; calibration data does not yet exist for this organization or GTM task.
uncertainties.impact: High for false approvals/escalation load; remain conservative and collect shadow data.

uncertainties.unknown: Exact common schema may change after implementation; multi-domain compatibility is unproven.
uncertainties.impact: Medium/high; keep v1alpha1 internal and avoid public plugin promises.

uncertainties.unknown: GTM vendor docs show intended features, not incremental pipeline/revenue outcomes or approval quality. Applicable privacy/marketing law varies by jurisdiction/channel.
uncertainties.impact: High; GTM stays draft-only and disabled until legal/value gates pass.

uncertainties.unknown: Cross-repository manifest/receipt design is proposed, not shown as one end-to-end feature by compared vendors.
Several official documents are living and may not expose stable publication/version dates.
uncertainties.impact: Medium for reproducibility; archive snapshots/commit hashes during implementation procurement.

uncertainties.unknown: GitLab composite identity and tool-governance behavior differ between runner flows and Agentic Chat and are version-specific; actual tenant defaults are unverified.
uncertainties.impact: High for authority isolation; require representative-principal and deny-default tests before use.

confidence.overall: Moderate-high for the recommended separation, gates and evidence discipline; moderate for exact shared schema; low-to-moderate for vendor ROI and cross-domain generality.

claim_level.documented product/workflow surfaces: high when supported by official docs, but availability/version must be confirmed
claim_level.WarpBench numeric report: high that Warp published the numbers; low that they generalize or establish causal quality-preserving ROI
claim_level.organizational productivity: low-to-moderate because internal anecdotes conflict with scoped independent evidence
claim_level.shared kernel design: moderate-high, triangulated with standards and prior validated studies but still a proposed synthesis
claim_level.GTM autonomy/value: low; controls are well supported, outcomes are not
claim_level.regulatory duties: high for cited general requirements, low for organization-specific legal applicability without counsel
